report_name: North Korean Group 'Sapphire Sleet' Behind Rust Supply-Chain Attack

threat_actors.name: Sapphire Sleet
threat_actors.description: A North Korean state-sponsored threat actor that conducted a sophisticated software supply-chain attack against the Rust programming language ecosystem by compromising a maintainer's account on crates.io and publishing malicious versions of popular libraries.
threat_actors.goals: To steal developer credentials, API keys, and other sensitive data for follow-on network intrusions, data breaches, and financial theft.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
attack_patterns.description: The attackers directly compromised the software supply chain by publishing malicious versions of trusted Rust libraries (arrayref, internment, and append-only-vec) on the official crates.io package registry.

attack_patterns.name: Match Legitimate Name or Location
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor used the typosquatted dependency name 'proc-macro1' to deceive developers into believing it was a legitimate procedural macro crate.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
attack_patterns.description: The attack leveraged the automated execution of a malicious build script (build.rs) during the 'cargo build' process to download and execute a second-stage payload.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials from Password Stores
attack_patterns.description: The final payload of the attack was designed to harvest sensitive information from compromised developer machines, including browser credentials and cryptocurrency wallets.

malware.name: proc-macro1
malware.description: A malicious, typosquatted Rust crate published to crates.io. It was included as a dependency in compromised legitimate packages and used a build.rs script to download a second-stage payload during compilation.

tools.name: cargo build
tools.description: The legitimate Rust build command was abused by the attackers to automatically fetch and execute the malicious 'proc-macro1' dependency's build script.

tools.name: arrayref
tools.description: A legitimate, popular Rust crate that was compromised by Sapphire Sleet. Version 0.3.10 was modified to include 'proc-macro1' as a malicious dependency.

tools.name: internment
tools.description: A legitimate, popular Rust crate that was compromised by Sapphire Sleet. Version 0.8.7 was modified to include 'proc-macro1' as a malicious dependency.

tools.name: append-only-vec
tools.description: A legitimate, popular Rust crate that was compromised by Sapphire Sleet. Version 0.1.9 was modified to include 'proc-macro1' as a malicious dependency.

identities.name: Rust developer community
identities.description: The target of the supply-chain attack, who would unknowingly use the compromised Rust libraries in their projects, leading to potential compromise of their machines and organizations.

infrastructure.name: crates.io Rust Package Registry
infrastructure.description: The official Rust package registry that was compromised by Sapphire Sleet to host and distribute malicious versions of popular libraries.

indicators.name: Malicious Rust Crate 'proc-macro1' Detection
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Malicious Rust Crate 'proc-macro1' File Artifact
id: 7c5b1a3d-8f9e-4b1c-8a7d-9e8f7a6b5c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects file artifacts related to the malicious Rust crate 'proc-macro1', indicative of the Sapphire Sleet supply-chain attack.
references:
  - https://cyberrecaps.com/news/cybersecurity-news-august-22-2026
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-23
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\.cargo\registry\src\github.com\proc-macro1-'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the presence of the malicious 'proc-macro1' crate in the local cargo registry cache.

indicators.name: Suspicious Rust Dependency 'proc-macro1' in Cargo.lock
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Rust Dependency 'proc-macro1' in Cargo.lock
id: 1d2e3f4a-5b6c-4d7e-8f9a-0b1c2d3e4f5a
status: experimental
description: Detects the string 'proc-macro1' within a 'Cargo.lock' file, which is a strong indicator of compromise by the Sapphire Sleet supply-chain attack.
references:
  - https://cyberrecaps.com/news/cybersecurity-news-august-22-2026
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-23
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'grep'
      - 'proc-macro1'
      - 'Cargo.lock'
  condition: selection
---
indicators.description: A hunting rule to find projects that have the malicious 'proc-macro1' dependency listed in their Cargo.lock file.
